pageCache.text:
Welcome to Life Skills Enterprise
Welcome to Life Skills Enterprise School.
Paul Barrett, Headteacher
Choosing the right school for your child is one of the most important decisions you will ever make. As both an Executive Principal and a father of a son with autism, I understand that decision from both a professional and a personal perspective.
Watching my own son grow into adulthood has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. Like many families, we have celebrated achievements that others may have taken for granted, overcome challenges together and seen first-hand how the right support, patience, belief and opportunities can transform a young person’s future. His journey continually reminds me that potential should never be limited by diagnosis.
That belief has shaped my career and continues to influence every decision we make at our Life Skills schools including Life Skills Enterprise. Our school was founded on a simple but powerful principle: every child deserves to be understood before they are taught. When young people feel safe, valued and genuinely believed in, they begin to develop the confidence to take risks, embrace challenges and discover what they are truly capable of achieving.
We are ambitious for every pupil. Academic progress matters, but so too do confidence, communication, resilience, emotional wellbeing, independence and preparing successfully for adult life. These are the foundations that enable our young people to thrive long after they leave our school.
Our dedicated staff work tirelessly to build trusting relationships with pupils and their families. We recognise that no two children are the same, which is why our approach is personalised, nurturing and aspirational. We celebrate every success, whether it is a first conversation, a qualification achieved, a return to education or a young person taking confident steps towards employment, further education or independent living.
I firmly believe that outstanding education changes lives. Not because it removes every barrier, but because it equips young people with the confidence, skills and self-belief to overcome them. It is an enormous privilege to lead Life Skills Enterprise School and to work alongside such a talented and committed team every day. Together, we strive to create an environment where every child feels they belong, every family feels supported and every young person is given the opportunity to fulfil their potential.
Thank you for visiting our website. I hope it provides a glimpse into the passion, care and ambition that define our school. I warmly invite you to visit us, meet our team and experience firsthand the welcoming community that makes Life Skills Enterprise School such a special place.
I look forward to welcoming you and your family.
Careers & Post-16 Preparation
Life Skills Enterprise is designed with careers and post-16 preparation in mind. It will offer a variety of therapies and interventions and also core curriculum subjects such as Maths and English in order to prepare young people for adulthood.
The Venue
The venue has huge scope to develop community links with its secret garden and excellent location with nearby businesses. This environment gives young people the chance to explore future pathways and venture into the world of work. The links with vocational job opportunities is strong, and being so close to the creative arts associated with Margate is something the school will definitely look to fully utilise.
The Provision
A provision to support the development of the whole child will allow children to flourish in a supportive environment where nurture flows through to resilience with the addition of skills for life.
Life Skills Enterprise are pleased that OFSTED have said the school is likely to meet all the independent school standards when it opens. Read the full report here.
Our Ethos
To provide a wholesome curriculum that provides core academic subjects and a focus on developing skills for life so students can flourish.

Vision, Mission & Curriculum Intent
© Life Skills Enterprise 2026 - All Rights Reserved | Website by

Curriculum Intent
At Life Skills Enterprise the overarching aim of the curriculum is that the students are fully prepared for their next steps in learning and towards adult life and that learning is relevant and enjoyable.
This is achieved with the use of a double stranded curriculum that encompasses both an emphasis on life skills and a more traditional academic curriculum.
We fundamentally believe that meeting students’ social and emotional needs, combined with academic achievement will increase their chances of becoming positive, independent, and resilient members of society.

Expression of Interest
There is an opportunity to have a tour of the facility and to meet with staff to give clear information about our school and the choices you have as a Parent, Carer or interested party for continuing Lifelong Learning for your child.
There is an opportunity to have a tour of the facility and to meet with staff.
To arrange a visit please contact us via email on rachel@lifeskillsenterprise.co.uk.
Or complete the short form as an expression of interest and your details are sent securely to us, after which we will be in touch with you.
© Life Skills Enterprise 2026 - All Rights Reserved | Website by

Subject Descriptors
Linguistic - Listening, Speaking, Reading and Writing
Linguistics and communication are the cornerstone of the curriculum at Life Skills Enterprise as the ability to express oneself is an essential life skill. This is delivered through English, which as a gateway subject, enables students to access the entire curriculum. English is taught in every class, across all key stages.
Since reading is key to future success in life, there is a distinct and targeted Literacy plan in place across the school, in line with the 2021 DfE Reading Framework. Reading and literacy sessions are completed by all children at all key stages. The students read, either as a class reader or individually which is recorded in their reading journals, and they take regular tests relating to what they have read.
All students also get the opportunity to access Modern Foreign Language workshops throughout the year which focus on French. Languages are also offered as an extra-curricular option to those students with an interest.
Mathematical
Our aim at Life Skills Enterprise is for students to enjoy mathematics and recognise the importance of it in their everyday life. They are encouraged to develop their confidence and develop a positive attitude towards the subject. All classes have maths at least five times a week.
Scientific
Science is taught across the curriculum at all key stages with an emphasis to evoke a sense of awe and wonder. We aim to stimulate curiosity and enjoyment in science and its methods of enquiry to demonstrate how the application of the subject can be useful in everyday life.
All students can complete experiments and are taught how to follow safety procedures.
Technological
All students have a laptop and are encouraged to use ICT is to ensure that they are equipped with a good working knowledge of the skills required to prepare their for future employment. All students also can gain basic cooking skills, delivered through the Wheel of Independence framework. This allows all students to have the chance to learn basic skills including knife work, food hygiene and following basic recipes. They also can deliver meals using the food that has been grown in the school allotment.
Human and Social
Students are taught to have an insight into people and places, how people live and how they interact with their environment, developing a sense of awe and wonder and providing them with an understanding of the world they live in.
Teachers organise educational visits and field trips where they will add value to their learning and provide the students with an opportunity to gather data and deepen their understanding of processes and events. Workshops also have a focus on deepening understanding of the past including the life of a Roman soldier.
Physical
Many students have negative connotations of physical exercise, so the focus of PE is participation and for students to really enjoy the activities. In turn, helping students develop key motor skills including control, coordination and improving their stamina and fitness. Students are also encouraged to develop moral values such as teamwork, fair play, resilience, and commitment. All students across all key stages have a double timetabled PE lesson every week. Lessons either take place in the various sport facilities that are on site or off site for specialist sports, including a local golf course, swimming pool and climbing centre.
Aesthetic and Creative
Art is highly regarded on the curriculum due to the therapeutic nature of the subject. It is delivered to all students, every week, across all classes. There is a focus on investigating artists, producing their own creative work, exploring their ideas and using different techniques including drawing, painting and sculpture.
Peripatetic music sessions are offered on a weekly basis by Kent Music to the students who have an interest. They can play guitar, drums or keyboard and can take part in an end of term performance. Several of the workshops also focus on music and culture, so that all students encounter music experiences.
Personal Development
There is a strong focus through the curriculum on Personal Development and it is imperative to the students at the Life Skills Enterprise to support them.
All students are taught PSHE, incorporating the new statutory guidance for sex, relationship, and health education in England. It is delivered in line with the strands of the PSHE Association and covers Social, Moral, Spiritual and Cultural (SMSC), Fundamental British Values (FBV) and Sex and Relationship Education (SRE). Online safety is also embedded into the PSHE curriculum, teaching students to be alert and aware of how to safely use ICT resources. Students are taught about how to recognise and avoid danger when using ICT resources and preventing themselves from cyber bullying and online exploitation. All students have a timetabled lesson every week.
All students complete weekly Duke of Edinburgh lessons (DofE), delivered by a highly experienced teacher. This allows them to start completing the formal qualifications, with the aim that all students leave the school with at least the Bronze Award.

Admissions
Life Skills Enterprise School provides full time education for boys and girls diagnosed with Autism. At full capacity the school will be a Secondary (10-18 years old) provision.
Pupils attending the school are referred via KCC and every effort is made to ensure that the child is appropriately placed and that the provision offered by the school matches the needs of the child.

Please contact the school via our website to find out the next dates. You can also register your interest by filling in our online expression of interest form.

Safeguarding at Life Skills Enterprise
At Life Skills Enterprise, safeguarding and promoting the welfare of every student is our highest priority. We are committed to ensuring that all students—each of whom has an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) — are protected, supported, and empowered to thrive in a safe and nurturing environment.
We recognise that our students may face additional vulnerabilities, and our safeguarding approach is tailored to meet their individual needs. This includes placing a strong emphasis on communication support, emotional wellbeing, structured care, and proactive intervention.
Our safeguarding practices are underpinned by:
Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE 2025)
Our Safeguarding Commitment includes:
We actively promote a culture of listening to students, with a strong focus on pupil voice. Staff are trained to recognise both verbal and non-verbal signs that may indicate a safeguarding concern.
If you have any concerns about a student’s safety or wellbeing, please contact our Designated Safeguarding Lead, Mickey Capeling, via the school office.
You can view our full Safeguarding and Child Protection Policy by clicking here.
Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) 2025
Life Skills Manor follow guidance from Keeping Children Safe in Education (KCSIE) 2025. You can see the UK Government guidance on www.gov.uk or download the PDF here.
Click the image to download the document or click here.
Together, we are committed to creating a safe, respectful, and empowering environment where every student can flourish.
The Parents’ Guide to Teaching Your Teen Online Safety
Online safety is near the top of the worry list for most parents today. More teens than ever are using social media channels on the daily, and they’re doing everything from learning to socialising, gaming to shopping.
CEOP
CEOP is a website run by the UK Police Force. It has a number of tools to help you make a report of online abuse and problems.
Thinkuknow
The National Crime Agency's CEOP Education team’s website to help protect children and young people from online child sexual abuse.
Marie Collins Foundation
Supporting victims and survivors, empowering families and professionals, and driving change to tackle technology-assisted child sexual abuse (TACSA).
Molly Rose Foundation
Working at the intersect of suicide prevention, online safety and tech accountability we exist to end preventable harm online and give young people the tools to live long and stay strong.
We are with you
With You is a charity providing free, confidential support to people experiencing issues with drugs, alcohol or mental health.
Childline
Childline is a charity who can help anyone under 19 in the UK with any issue they’re going through. You can talk about anything. Whether it’s something big or small, their trained counsellors are here to support you.
Educate against hate
A website to provide practical advice, support and resources to protect children from extremism and radicalisation.
Family lives
Targeted early intervention and family support.
Kent and Youth Child Health
A team who work to improve the general health and wellbeing of children, young people and their families to support children to get the best start in life.
Kooth Home
Online mental wellbeing community.
Parent Zone
An online resource to improve outcomes for children in an increasingly digital world. It provides support and information to parents, children and schools, working globally to help families to navigate the internet safely and confidently.
Kent Resilience Hub
Supporting young people to cope better with the pressures of everyday life.
